subject: Linguistics
title: Borrowing and Loanwords
description: A fast breakdown of Borrowing and Loanwords for builders.

hook.text: 'Kindergarten,' 'sushi,' 'safari'—English borrows words from everywhere and keeps them.

buildup.text: Borrowing occurs when one language adopts words from another—usually through cultural contact.

discovery.text: English has absorbed from French (beef), Norse (sky), Arabic (algebra), and Hindi (jungle).

twist.text: Borrowed words often change meaning: French 'entrée' means starter, but in American English it means main course.

climax.text: Some languages actively resist borrowing—French and Icelandic create native alternatives.

punchline.text: Languages borrow freely—and make the words their own.
